# Generic summer city dataset — revised research handoff

The user selected Dallas, Boston and Phoenix and authorized generic summer numbers, with one value per city-based field. This revision uses **full-day June–August means** from the **2001–2025 NASA POWER gridded climatology**. It is not a particular observed day, an afternoon design condition, or an extreme-heat test. The dataset explicitly labels its values as gridded climatological estimates. [user_2026_city_scope; nasa_nd_climatology_api; nasa_nd_meteorology]

## City comparison

| City | Air temperature (°C) | Relative humidity (%) | Surface pressure (Pa) | Outdoor wind at 10 m (m/s) | Daily horizontal solar energy (kWh/m²/day) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Dallas | 29.2 | 62.0 | 99230.0 | 3.86 | 6.66 |
| Boston | 21.1 | 75.9 | 100560.0 | 1.88 | 5.66 |
| Phoenix | 33.0 | 26.8 | 95350.0 | 2.86 | 7.62 |

Each city's table values cite nasa_2026_dallas_climatology, nasa_2026_boston_climatology or nasa_2026_phoenix_climatology respectively, at properties.parameter.{T2M,RH2M,PS,WS10M,ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN}.{JUN,JUL,AUG}. Exact request URLs and source snapshots are in city_climate_manifest.csv and city_climate_sources/. Monthly source values and record IDs are retained in city_climate_monthly_provenance.csv.

## Definitions and calculation

Each summer value is (30 × June + 31 × July + 31 × August) / 92. Surface pressure is then converted from kPa to Pa by multiplying by 1000. Temperature and humidity are reported to one decimal, pressure to the nearest ten pascals, wind and daily solar energy to two decimals. A precision setting of -1 in derivation metadata means rounding to tens. This rounding does not claim measurement accuracy. All three required source months are present for all selected variables. The averaging is explicitly authorized by the request for generic summer inputs; no missing observation was filled or interpolated.

The API response identifies a 2001–2025 climatology and API v2.10.1. That response metadata is retained rather than replacing it with an older documentation example period. Weather query locations are the documented coordinates of Dallas/Fort Worth International, Boston Logan and Phoenix Sky Harbor reference stations. Those are reproducible city-area anchors chosen for this generic comparison, not selected cooling venues. NWS metadata supplies coordinates only; the weather values come from NASA's grid, not airport instruments. [nws_2026_dallas_location; nws_2026_boston_location; nws_2026_phoenix_location; corresponding nasa_2026_*_climatology records]

NASA describes the meteorology as MERRA-2 gridded estimates on a native 0.5° latitude by 0.625° longitude grid. Model-grid elevation and actual station elevation differ and are retained separately. Pressure is surface pressure at the model grid, without a venue-elevation adjustment. Temperature and RH are at 2 m; wind is at 10 m. The time basis is solar local time, without a daylight-saving clock conversion. [nasa_nd_meteorology, MERRA-2 section; city response geometry and parameter definitions]

Solar energy is a daily total per horizontal area, averaged across summer days, not instantaneous irradiance or radiation incident on a person. The API's T2M_MAX and T2M_MIN fields were retrieved but are not used: their extrema must not be mislabeled as a typical day's high and low. The full original responses are retained for audit.

Mean temperature and mean RH are separate marginal summaries, not a measured simultaneous air state. Any later comfort calculation at these means is a synthetic generic-condition calculation; it does not equal average summer comfort or establish heatwave safety. Wind at 10 m does not fill body-level airspeed. No mean radiant temperature, local ventilation rate, occupancy, equipment airflow, water use, tariff, cost or owner limit was inferred from the city names.

## What changed in the registers

City-dependent requirements now have separate Dallas, Boston and Phoenix records. Applicable climate means replace the former blank outdoor temperature, RH and pressure fields. Pressure-basis metadata is also populated. Global proposal values and implementation choices remain global so the same number is not counted three times. Missing city-dependent inputs remain blank separately for each city. Original venue-role placeholder slots are superseded by the three selected city scopes; no bus/rail/real-venue role mapping has been invented.

analysis_ready_inputs.csv retains every unresolved required record. The verified_derived status on climate summaries means the source and arithmetic were checked; data_kind still identifies them as modeled climatology, not verified_measured. The user's generic-city authorization is recorded alongside them. Physical site data remain needed for a venue-specific analysis.

The original attachment contains 94 collection/responsibility rows plus four option rows, despite its statement that there are 231. All 94 remain mapped in checklist_coverage.csv; the original text is preserved unchanged. Source examples remain in candidate_evidence.csv and are not city inputs. Monte Carlo and interpolation remain disabled. No thermal, comfort, efficiency or minimax-regret model was run.

## Remaining inputs

The full missing_inputs.csv retains city-specific equipment/geometry/occupancy/measurement gaps and the deferred global choices. Generic climate resolves the need to choose a real study date for this summary. It does not define study hours, occupied duration, local shelter conditions or economic tariffs. The owner can keep equipment and criteria unresolved as previously requested. SET, person-degree-hour cooling benefit, resource feasibility and minimax-regret decisions cannot yet run defensibly.

## Complete data register

The records below reproduce the full CSV schema. Numeric blanks are deliberate. Source monthly values are linked by input_record_ids; no single raw scalar original_value exists for a three-month aggregation, so the original inputs are preserved in the linked provenance file instead.
